card.title: Formal Letter Writing — editor, application, complaint, inquiry

rows.label: Concept
rows.text: **What it is:** a letter to someone you do NOT know (editor, manager, office). Half the marks are the fixed BLOCK LAYOUT; the other half is polite business tone.

rows.label: Formula
rows.text:
Trick 1: Formats earn marks — letter to the editor: sender's address, date, editor's address, salutation 'Sir/Madam', subject line, body (problem→effects→request), 'Yours faithfully'; job application adds CV reference…
Trick 2: Complaint letters: state the FACT (what, when, where), the LOSS, and the REMEDY you want — three paragraphs, no emotion without evidence.

rows.label: Conditions
rows.text: **Tone grammar:** no contractions (*do not*, *I am*); polite modals (*would*, *could*, *may*); passive voice for formality ('the matter is being investigated').  ·  **Variants:** *Editor* (public issue + call for action), *Job application* (post + skills + 'Enclosure: CV'), *Complaint* (what, when, defect + remedy + deadline), *Inquiry/Order* (price/availability/terms).

rows.label: Special cases
rows.text: **Full guide:** Full model answers, starting-line banks and exam tips: [/knowledge/writing](/knowledge/writing).  ·  **Formal letter anatomy (classified)** | Part | Position | Function | |---|---|---| | Sender’s address | Top right/left | Reply route | | Date | Below address | Record | | Receiver + address | Left | Exact destination | | Subject line | After salutation | One-line purpose | | Body | 3 paragraphs | Why → what → ask | | Complimentary close | Right | Yours faithfully/sincerely |

rows.label: Solved
rows.text: Q. Write a letter to the editor about road accidents in your town. (4 marks) — format + problem with one example + two causes + two suggestions.

rows.label: Limitation
rows.text: **Which close with which salutation** | Salutation | Close | Use when | |---|---|---| | Dear Sir/Madam | Yours faithfully | Name unknown | | Dear Mr Sharma | Yours sincerely | Name known | | Dear Editor | Yours sincerely/faithfully | Letters page |  ·  ```svg Formal letter: address ladder to the ask <svg viewBox="0 0 640 200" font-family="Segoe UI" font-size="13"><rect x="0" y="0" width="640" height="200" fill="#ffffff"/><g text-anchor="middle"><g font-size="12"><rect x="150" y="35" width="340" height="24" rx="6" fill="#eff6ff" stroke="#1d4ed8"/><text x="320" y="51" fill="#1d4ed8">addresses + date</text><rect x="150" y="66" width="340" height="24" rx="6"…

rows.label: Derivation
rows.text: **Block order:** Sender's address → Date → Recipient's designation + address → Subject line → Salutation ('Dear Sir/Madam') → Body (3 short paragraphs: who you are + purpose / details / polite request) → Complimentary close → Signature + full name in capitals.  ·  **The pairing rule that trips everyone:** 'Dear Sir/Madam' → end **Yours faithfully**; 'Dear Mr/Ms Sharma' (real name) → end **Yours sincerely**.

rows.label: Shortcut
rows.text: Trick 3: Subject line and 'Yours faithfully/truly' choice (faithfully when 'Dear Sir') — the two format details most students lose.

rows.label: Board question
rows.text: Q. What goes in the subject line of a complaint letter? (1 mark) — a concise statement of the complaint, e.g. 'Complaint about frequent power cuts'.

rows.label: Hints
rows.text: **Variants:** *Editor* (public issue + call for action), *Job application* (post + skills + 'Enclosure: CV'), *Complaint* (what, when, defect + remedy + deadline), *Inquiry/Order* (price/availability/terms).
